lesson.title: Ask before it acts
lesson.subtitle: Agents, the tools they hold, and a person's yes

video.title: Ask before it acts
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (main character)
Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Cards: Reads the timetable; Messages parents; Nobody approved it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Our school tried an AI agent that could read the timetable and send messages to parents. It was meant to send reminders. One day it sent the whole parent list a message nobody had approved.

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: agents that act, the tools we give them, and the yes that keeps them safe.

scenes.visual: Two columns. Chatbot: Only talks. Agent: Reads the timetable; Sets reminders; Sends messages.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A chatbot only talks. An AI agent can also use tools: read a timetable, check attendance, set a reminder, send a message. That makes it useful, and it raises the stakes.

scenes.visual: Two columns. Reading tools: Timetable, library; Worst case: a leak. Acting tools: Send, delete, pay; Can be turned on you.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Tools come in two kinds. Reading tools look things up; at worst, they leak something. Acting tools change things: send, delete, pay, publish. A tricked agent with an acting tool can act against you.

scenes.visual: A list: The fewest tools for the job; Reading before acting; For the shortest time; A small blast radius.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The rule is least privilege: give an agent the fewest tools its job needs, reading before acting, for the shortest time. Everything a tampered result could reach is the blast radius. Keep it small.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! An agent's job is to plan tomorrow's lessons from the timetable and the library. Which tools should it get?

scenes.visual: A list: Timetable; Library; Hidden orders can't act; Worst case: it talks.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: No acting tool, nothing to turn
scenes.narration: Timetable and library only. With no acting tool, a hidden order in a result can't make it send or delete anything. The worst it can do is read or talk.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A person's yes, checked in code
scenes.narration: For jobs that must act, add a person's yes. Before any message is sent, the agent shows it and asks. And the code checks: was it asked for, and did someone approve this exact message? The model can't skip that step.

scenes.visual: A list: Prompt rules can be faked; A fake “Shall I send?”; Code knows who asked.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Why in code, and not just in the prompt? A hidden order can fake an approval question, and a trusting yes may send it. Code that knows who really asked can't be fooled by words.

scenes.visual: A list: Every action; Who approved it; And when; See what went wrong.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Keep a log, too. Every action the agent takes, with who approved it and when. If something goes wrong, you can see what happened and fix it.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: Grant tools; Tampered results; Count the harm; Fewer tools, again.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: only what it needs
scenes.narration: In the app, pick a job and grant the agent some tools. Then set a batch of tampered results loose on it, and count the harmful actions. Take tools away, and run it again.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. An agent must tell parents the date of the school trip. What keeps that safe?

scenes.visual: The summary: Reading tools vs acting tools; The fewest tools; A person's yes, in code; Keep a log. Takeaway: The fewer tools it holds, the less a trick can do.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.on_screen_text: Reading or acting · Fewest tools · Ask · Log
scenes.narration: Only the tool it needs, and a yes checked in code. Remember: reading tools leak at worst; acting tools can be turned against you. Give the fewest tools, and keep the blast radius small. Ask before it acts, and keep a log.

scenes.visual: A list: Design a helper robot; Only the tools it needs; Mark the tools that act; Who says yes?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: make “permission slips for robots”. Groups design a class helper robot for one job, and list only the tools it needs. Mark every tool that acts, and decide who must say yes before it does.

checkpoints.prompt: An agent's job is to plan tomorrow's lessons from the timetable and the library. Which tools should it get?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Right: two reading tools are all the job needs.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: extra tools only add to what a trick could reach. Give it just timetable and library.

checkpoints.prompt: An agent must tell parents the date of the school trip. What keeps that safe?

options.text: Give it every tool so it never gets stuck
Only the send tool, and a person's yes, checked in code
Tell it in the prompt to be careful

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes: one tool for the job, and a yes the model can't fake.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: more tools mean more risk, and a prompt can be talked round. Use one tool and a checked yes.
